\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سہارا} (sahārā)}{سہارا (sahārā)}]{\ur{سہارا} (sahārā) — a support; someone to lean on}

\label{lesson:UR-C374-sahara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to set (of the sun), then the Urdu for unfinished.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سہارا}}
\textbf{\ur{سہارا}} — \emph{sahārā} — \textquotedblleft{}a support; someone to lean on\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{کا} \ur{سہارا} \ur{نہ} \ur{ہوتا} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{گر} \ur{جاتا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp kā sahārā na hotā to maiṅ gir jātā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you had not held me up, I would have fallen.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سہارا}} (\emph{sahārā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{sahārā}, \textquotedblleft{}help\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{sahakāra}, \textquotedblleft{}assistance\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13299).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sahārā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sahārā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āp kā sahārā na hotā to maiṅ gir jātā.} — If you had not held me up, I would have fallen.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to set (of the sun), then the Urdu for unfinished, then say \emph{sahārā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{سہارا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A support; someone to lean on\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ضد} (zid)}{ضد (zid)}]{\ur{ضد} (zid) — stubbornness; insistence}

\label{lesson:UR-C374-zid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for unfinished, then the Urdu for someone to lean on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ضد}}
\textbf{\ur{ضد}} — \emph{zid} — \textquotedblleft{}stubbornness; insistence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{نے} \ur{ضد} \ur{کی} \ur{تو} \ur{کچھ} \ur{نہیں} \ur{ملے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum ne zid kī to kuchh nahīṅ mile gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you are stubborn, you will get nothing.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ضد}} (\emph{zid}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḍidd}, \textquotedblleft{}the opposite\textquotedblright{}; Urdu uses it for stubborn insistence, a sense our sources do not trace.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zid}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum ne zid kī to kuchh nahīṅ mile gā.} — If you are stubborn, you will get nothing.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for unfinished, then the Urdu for someone to lean on, then say \emph{zid} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{انحصار} (inhisār)}{انحصار (inhisār)}]{\ur{انحصار} (inhisār) — reliance; dependence}

\label{lesson:UR-C374-inhisar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for stubbornness, then the Urdu for eligible.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{انحصار}}
\textbf{\ur{انحصار}} — \emph{inhisār} — \textquotedblleft{}reliance; dependence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{انحصار} \ur{صرف} \ur{بارش} \ur{پر} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{مشکل} \ur{ہو} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar inhisār sirf bārish par hai to mushkil ho gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If everything depends on the rain alone, things will be hard.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{انحصار}} (\emph{inhisār}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{inḥiṣār}, \textquotedblleft{}being confined, being limited\textquotedblright{}, of the same family as \textbf{\ur{منحصر}}, \textquotedblleft{}depending\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اصرار} \ur{کرنا} (isrār karnā)}{اصرار کرنا (isrār karnā)}]{\ur{اصرار} \ur{کرنا} (isrār karnā) — to insist}

\label{lesson:UR-C374-israr-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for eligible, then the Urdu for reliance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اصرار} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{اصرار} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{isrār karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to insist\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{اصرار} \ur{کرتے} \ur{ہیں} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{آؤں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp isrār karte haiṅ to maiṅ āūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you insist, I will come.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{آنے} \ur{پر} \ur{اصرار} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne āne par isrār kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اصرار} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{isrār karnā}) is built from \emph{isrār}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{iṣrār}, \textquotedblleft{}persisting\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}
